p1.realBugIfLapsed: If !_initPromise is mutated to true (always), a new init promise would be created on every request even when one already exists. This causes double-init attempts — performance issue, not security. In practice, _middleware is set after first init, so the outer if (!_middleware && !_initFailed) prevents re-entry. The mutant is largely equivalent due to the outer guard.
p1.whySurvived: The outer if (!_middleware && !_initFailed) guard means that once _middleware is set, the inner if (!_initPromise) is never reached. The mutant only matters during the brief window between first request and init completion — and _initPromise is set synchronously before any await, so the window is effectively zero.
p1.recommendedTest: should not create a new _initPromise when one already exists (verify promise identity is preserved across concurrent requests)
